questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Coefficient in a 3x3 Linear System Using Cramer's Rule
questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}19x+3y-4z=-2 \\ 6x+ky-4z=-1 \\ -9x-y+2z=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that  $y=21$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $2k+20,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}19 & 3 & -4 \\ 6 & k & -4 \\ -9 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|=2k+20\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}19 & -2 & -4 \\ 6 & -1 & -4 \\ -9 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}| & =19\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -4 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}|-(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & -4 \\ -9 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-4)\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & -1 \\ -9 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =19(-2+20)+2(12-36)-4(30-9) \\  & =342-48-84 \\  & =210.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{210}{2k+20}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $y=21.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{210}{2k+20} & =21 \\ 10 & =2k+20 \\ 2k & =-10 \\ k & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+2y+z=1 \\ 5x+3y+4z=2 \\ x+y-z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-1,$ then $x=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+2y+1z=1 \\ 5x+3y+4z=2 \\ 1x+1y+(-1)z=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3-4)-2(-2-4)+(2-3) \\  & =-7+12-1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{4}{-1}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+5z=-1 \\ 2x+3y+2z=0 \\ x+4y=k\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $x=-4$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $15,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}|=15\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 \\ k & 4 & 0\end{aligned}| & =-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ k & 0\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ k & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(0-8)+(0-2k)+5(0-3k) \\  & =8-2k-15k \\  & =8-17k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{8-17k}{15}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=-4.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8-17k}{15} & =-4 \\ 8-17k & =-60 \\ -17k & =-68 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-5y-2z=-7 \\ 2x+y-4z=-10 \\ 3x-3y-2z=-7\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $16,$ then $z=$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+(-5)y+(-2z)=-7 \\ 2x+1y+(-4)z=-10 \\ 3x+(-3)y+(-2)z=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -2\end{aligned}|=16.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{z}$, we replace the third column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}3 & -5 & -7 \\ 2 & 1 & -10 \\ 3 & -3 & -7\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -10 \\ -3 & -7\end{aligned}|-(-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -10 \\ 3 & -7\end{aligned}|+(-7)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(-7-30)+5(-14+30)-7(-6-3) \\  & =-111+80+63 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{32}{16}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-4y-5z=1 \\ 2x+3y-3z=k \\ -5x+3y+7z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $y=-1$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-19,$ find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & -5 \\ 2 & 3 & -3 \\ -5 & 3 & 7\end{aligned}|=-19\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y}=|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -5 \\ 2 & k & -3 \\ -5 & -2 & 7\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -3 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -5 & 7\end{aligned}|+(-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ -5 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(7k-6)-(14-15)-5(-4+5k) \\  & =21k-18+1+20-25k \\  & =-4k+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D}=\frac{-4k+3}{-19}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $y=-1.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-4k+3}{-19} & =-1 \\ -4k+3 & =19 \\ -4k & =16 \\ k & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$
